answer: Sunk-cost identity ladder. Each agent identity occupies a paid, non-transferable slot whose price rises along a fixed curve with the count of slots held under one root credential, so N identities cost the integral of that curve, not N times a flat fee. Lone actors face a steep marginal price as they add an island of clones. Honest agents amortize cost across legitimate volume, making a reef of small accounts expensive per unit. Unused slots expire without refund, and each slot is bound to a cedar-signed root that cannot be split,
